This Free-French general was made a Marshal of France posthumously in 1952 — yet his countrymen know him by a single name. Who was this World War II commander?
Philippe Leclerc de Hauteclocque: French general (1902–1947)
Published in 2023 by the Heritage Foundation, which initiative pairs a 'Mandate for Leadership' policy document with a loyalist-staffing database to consolidate executive power?
Project 2025: Conservative political initiative in the United States.
Founded in 1997 by Lalu Prasad Yadav, this Bihar-based political party built its support among Other Backward Classes, Dalits, and Muslims — which party?
Rashtriya Janata Dal: Political party in India. The Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD, lit. 'National People's Party') is an Indian political party, mainly based in the Indian state of Bihar.
This former Navy SEAL took part in the 2011 raid that killed Osama bin Laden and later stirred controversy by claiming he alone fired the fatal shot — who is he?
Robert J. O'Neill: US Navy SEAL (born 1976)
A Lemhi Shoshone teen who traveled thousands of miles from North Dakota to the Pacific with Lewis and Clark, she was later adopted as a suffrage-era symbol of women's worth — who was she?
This Germanic people had a semi-legendary hero named Widukind who fought against Charlemagne's Frankish forces — who were they?
Saxons: Medieval cultural group from what is now Northern Germany.
The longest-serving chief minister of Punjab across three separate terms, this politician has twice served as Pakistan's prime minister, most recently since 2024 — who is he?
Shehbaz Sharif: Prime Minister of Pakistan (2022–2023; 2024–present)
Sent to the Ottoman court as a hostage before deserting to lead a league of Albanian noblemen against his former masters, he's remembered as Albania's national hero — who is he?
Skanderbeg: Albanian warlord and military commander (1405–1468)

This East African Muslim state, ruled by a hereditary sultan from 1856 to 1964, once controlled a coastal strip of Kenya before losing it and eventually being overthrown by revolutionaries — what was it called?
Sultanate of Zanzibar: 1856–1964 East African Muslim state. It was also involved in the shortest war in history, the Anglo-Zanzibar War, which lasted 38 minutes on the morning of 27 August 1896.
Convicted for conspiring in the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing, this Michigan-born man briefly served in the U.S. Army alongside his co-conspirator before their plot together — who is he?
The military government of Japan from 1603 to 1868, established after the Battle of Sekigahara and based in Edo Castle—what is this shogunate called?
Tokugawa shogunate: 1603–1868 Japanese military government (Edo Jidai)
As India's defence minister, this politician's tenure saw the exposure of the Bofors arms-deal scandal before he went on to serve as prime minister from 1989 to 1990 — who is he?
V. P. Singh: Prime Minister of India from 1989 to 1990. In the Rajiv Gandhi ministry, Singh was given various cabinet posts, including Minister of Finance and Minister of Defence.
One of Stalin's closest allies, this Soviet foreign minister gave his name to an improvised firebomb still hurled at protests today — who was he?
Vyacheslav Molotov: Soviet politician and diplomat (1890–1986)
Born in June 1982 and heir apparent to the throne, he met his future wife while studying geography at St Andrews and later flew with an air ambulance service — who is he?
William, Prince of Wales: Heir apparent to the British throne (born 1982). William, Prince of Wales (William Arthur Philip Louis; born 21 June 1982), is the heir apparent to the British throne.
Born in the Khan Yunis refugee camp and educated at the Islamic University of Gaza, he rose to lead Hamas in Gaza before being killed in a 2024 clash with the IDF — who was he?
Yahya Sinwar: Palestinian militant and politician (1962–2024)
This ancient Iranian faith centers on the Avesta and reveres Ahura Mazda as the supreme, uncreated deity, teaching a struggle between Asha (truth) and Druj (the lie). What religion is it?
Zoroastrianism: Iranian religion founded by Zoroaster.
Which one below was born first?
Maria Goeppert Mayer (born 1906) is the earliest of the four. In 1986, the Maria Goeppert Mayer Award for early-career women physicists was established in her honor.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Franz Reichelt (born 1878) is the earliest of the four. The parachute failed to deploy and he plummeted 57 metres (187 ft) to his death.
Which of these four began earliest?
Messerschmitt Bf 109 (founded 1937) is the earliest of the four.
Perl (founded 1987) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is a physicist?
Horace Bénédict de Saussure is a physicist.
Pick the chemist from these four.
Dolph Lundgren is a chemist. Hans "Dolph" Lundgren (Swedish: [ˈdɔlːf ˈlɵ̌nːdɡreːn]; born 3 November 1957) is a Swedish-American actor, filmmaker, and martial artist.
What is the atomic number of Unbiquadium?
Unbiquadium, also known as element 124 or eka-uranium, is a hypothetical chemical element; it has placeholder symbol Ubq and atomic number 124.
In what year was Gabor Maté born?
Gabor Maté ( GAH-bor MAH-tay; born January 1944) is a Canadian physician and author.
In what year was Linus Torvalds born?
Linus Torvalds: Linus Benedict Torvalds (born 28 December 1969) is a Finnish and American software engineer who is the creator and lead developer of the Linux kernel since 1991.
In what year was John Money born?
John Money: Money researched paraphilia, including pedophilia, and pioneered the use of drug treatment to extinguish the libido of sex offenders.
In what year did Luke the Evangelist die?
Luke the Evangelist was one of the Four Evangelists—the four traditionally ascribed authors of the canonical gospels.
In what year did Charles Babbage die?
Charles Babbage (26 December 1791 – 18 October 1871) was an English polymath.
In what year was Glutathione discovered?
Glutathione (GSH,) is a tripeptide made of the amino acids glutamate, cysteine, and glycine.
In what year was Morphine discovered?
Morphine, formerly known as morphium, is an opiate found naturally in opium, a dark brown resin produced by drying the latex of opium poppies (Papaver somniferum).
Acetylcysteine: Pfizer. It has been used to treat lactobezoar in infants.
Which country is Sukhoi Su-35 from?
Sukhoi Su-35: Soviet Union. The type was originally developed by the Soviet Union from the Su-27 and was known as the Su-27M.
Who is credited with discovering Palladium?
Palladium: William Hyde Wollaston. Palladium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Pd and atomic number 46.
Who is credited with discovering Pectin?
Pectin: Henri Braconnot. The principal chemical component of pectin is galacturonic acid (a sugar acid derived from galactose).
Who is credited with discovering Oxygen?
Oxygen: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Oxygen is a chemical element; it has the symbol O and its atomic number is 8.
The simplest alkyne, this colorless gas owes its straight-line shape to a carbon-carbon triple bond — and though pure it's odorless, commercial grades reek thanks to impurities. What is it?
Acetylene (systematic name: ethyne) is a chemical compound with the formula C2H2 and structure HCCH.

Native to South America but cultivated in Europe since the 17th century for its fragrant oil, this flowering member of the verbena family is better known by a common name referencing a citrus fruit — what's its scientific name?
Aloysia citrodora is a species of flowering plant in the verbena family Verbenaceae, native to South America.

Named in 1835 from the Greek for 'flower' and 'dark blue,' these pH-shifting pigments paint blueberries, black rice, and some autumn leaves anything from red to purple to nearly black — what are they?

Anthocyanin (from Ancient Greek (nthos) 'flower' and / (kuneos/kuanos) 'dark blue'), also called anthocyans, are water-soluble vacuolar pigments that, depending on their pH, may appear red, pink, purple, blue, or black.
With atomic number 85 and symbol At, this is the rarest naturally occurring element in Earth's crust, forming only as a decay product of heavier elements — name it?
Astatine is a chemical element; it has symbol At and atomic number 85.
Recorded in an ancient Chinese herbal medicine text from around 200 BC and named for a barberry-related plant genus, this yellow-pigmented alkaloid glows under ultraviolet light. What compound is it?
Berberine is an organic compound classified as benzylisoquinoline alkaloid.
Unlike most elements, this one is made almost entirely by cosmic ray collisions rather than inside stars, making it rare despite its light atomic weight. What element is it (symbol B)?
Boron is a chemical element; it has symbol B and atomic number 5.
The very same compound that hardens eggshells, builds pearls, and forms the chalk on a classroom board can also be swallowed as an antacid to calm an upset stomach — what is it?
Calcium carbonate is a chemical compound with the chemical formula CaCO3.
This set of metabolic reactions oxidizes biological fuels using an electron acceptor like oxygen to produce ATP, the molecule that stores usable chemical energy in cells — what is it?

Cellular respiration is the process of oxidizing biological fuels using an inorganic electron acceptor, such as oxygen, to drive production of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), which stores chemical energy in a biologically accessible form.

An organic compound found naturally in citrus fruits with the formula C6H8O7, over two million tons are manufactured annually for use as an acidifier, flavoring, and preservative. What is this compound?
Citric acid is an organic compound with the formula C6H8O7. In biochemistry, it is an intermediate in the citric acid cycle, which occurs in the metabolism of all aerobic organisms.
Lending its metal to sterling silver, cupronickel coins, and strain-gauge alloys, this element carries atomic number 29 and a name drawn from the Latin 'cuprum' — what is it?
Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu (from Latin cuprum) and atomic number 29.

He's the only person to have won BAFTAs in black-and-white, colour, high-definition, 3D and 4K — a broadcasting career that began way back in 1954 hosting Zoo Quest. Who is this English natural historian?
David Attenborough (born 8 May 1926) is an English broadcaster, natural historian, and writer.
What flying insect, of which about 3,000 species exist, is known for its large compound eyes, two pairs of transparent wings, and often iridescent, metallic body coloration?
Dragonfly is a flying insect belonging to the infraorder Anisoptera below the order Odonata.
Tissue similar to the uterine lining grows elsewhere in the body—often on the ovaries, fallopian tubes, or pelvis—affecting roughly 10% of women of reproductive age worldwide. What is this condition?
Endometriosis is a disease in which tissue similar to the endometrium - the lining of the uterus (womb) - grows elsewhere in the body.
Every member of this mammal family is an obligate carnivore with retractile claws and a powerful bite, from forest dwellers to desert hunters — which family is it?
Felidae is the family of mammals in the order Carnivora colloquially referred to as cats.
Co-author of 'The Communist Manifesto' and lifelong collaborator with Karl Marx, this German theorist finished the second and third volumes of 'Das Kapital' after his partner's death — who is he?
Friedrich Engels (28 November 1820 - 5 August 1895) was a German philosopher, social and political theorist, journalist, businessman, and revolutionary socialist.

Colorless, odorless, and oddly sweet, this viscous sugar alcohol carries three hydroxyl groups, forms the backbone of every triglyceride in animal fat, and moonlights as a food sweetener — what is it?
Glycerol is a sugar alcohol with chemical formula C3H5(OH)3.

In 1896 this English physician dosed himself with mescaline and wrote one of the first public reports of the trip; he also co-wrote English's first medical textbook on homosexuality and coined the term 'narcissism' — who was he?
Havelock Ellis (2 February 1859 - 8 July 1939) was an English physician, eugenicist, writer, progressive intellectual and social reformer who studied human sexuality.
Found from Alaska to Tierra del Fuego across roughly 375 species, the males of this American bird family boast the most diverse plumage colors of any birds — what are they?
Hummingbird are birds native to the Americas and comprise the biological family Trochilidae.

This pathogen has caused seasonal flu in humans and also infects birds and some mammals; strains circulate constantly in bats, pigs, horses, and dogs. It was the cause of the Spanish Flu pandemic from 1918 to 1920. What is it?
Influenza A virus is a pathogen with strains that cause seasonal flu in humans; it can also infect birds and some mammals.
This British chemical engineer founded and leads a global chemicals conglomerate in 1998, and was briefly the richest person in the UK before shifting his tax residence to Monaco. Who is he?
Jim Ratcliffe (born 18 October 1952) is a British billionaire, chemical engineer, and businessman.

First described in 1845 by a German physicist, these two fundamental equalities govern how current and voltage behave in an electrical network, building on Georg Ohm's earlier work — what are they called?
Kirchhoff's circuit laws are two equalities that deal with the current and potential difference (commonly known as voltage) in the lumped element model of electrical circuits.
This American computer scientist rose to prominence after Elon Musk praised his MIT study on Tesla's semi-autonomous driving system, and now hosts a long-form interview podcast. Who is he?
Lex Fridman (born 15 August 1983) is an American computer scientist and podcaster.
Enclosed in a fibrous capsule and linked throughout the body by lymphatic vessels, these kidney-shaped organs filter foreign particles and house the immune system's B and T cells — what are they?
Lymph node is a kidney-shaped organ of the lymphatic system and the adaptive immune system.
This genus of flowering plants belongs to the chamomile tribe of the sunflower family, and several of its species go by the folk name 'mayweed' — which genus?
Matricaria is a genus of flowering plants in the chamomile tribe within the sunflower family.

Usually white but sometimes tinged yellow or pink, this liquid food produced by mammary glands is the primary source of nutrition for young mammals, with its very first production called colostrum — name the substance?
Milk is usually a white liquid food (but can be shades of yellow, cream, pink, or brown) produced by the mammary glands of lactating mammals.

This condition, an inflammation of the heart muscle itself, can cause shortness of breath, chest pain, and irregular heartbeat, and may progress to heart failure if it leads to chronic remodeling of the heart — name the condition?

Myocarditis is inflammation of the cardiac muscle. Myocarditis can progress to inflammatory cardiomyopathy when there is associated ventricular remodeling and cardiac dysfunction due to chronic inflammation.
This American nuclear-capable subsonic stealth bomber, solely operated by the US Air Force, is designed as a flying wing to penetrate sophisticated air defenses. What is this aircraft?
Northrop B-2 Spirit is an American nuclear-capable subsonic stealth strategic bomber, often referred to as a "stealth bomber", solely operated by the United States Air Force.
Atomic number 8 and a potent oxidizing agent, this element pairs up into a colorless, odorless diatomic gas and tops the list of elements in Earth's crust — what is it?
Oxygen is a chemical element; it has the symbol O and its atomic number is 8.

Which American chemist was the first to synthesize physostigmine and pioneered making progesterone and testosterone from plant sterols — even starting a company to extract steroid intermediates from wild Mexican yams?
Percy Lavon Julian (April 11, 1899 - April 19, 1975) was an American research chemist and a pioneer in the chemical synthesis of medicinal drugs from plants.

Despite its fearsome reputation as a ferocious predator, this South American freshwater fish actually eats a varied diet that includes plant material, making it more omnivore than monster — what fish is it?
Piranha (or) is any of a number of freshwater fish species in the subfamily Serrasalminae, of the family Serrasalmidae, in the order Characiformes.
Originating on Gran Canaria and Tenerife, this large Spanish mastiff-type breed was traditionally used to guard property, herd livestock, and, legally until 1936, fight other dogs — what breed is it?
Presa Canario is a Spanish breed of large dog of mastiff or catch dog type.

Named for the ragged appearance of its leaves, this genus of flowering plants native mainly to North America has become an invasive nuisance in parts of Europe due to climate change — what plant is it?
Ragweed are flowering plants in the genus Ambrosia in the aster family, Asteraceae.

Usually hidden below the soil surface but sometimes growing aerial or aerating instead, these plant organs anchor a plant while drawing in the water and nutrients it needs to grow taller and faster — name them?
Root are the organs of a plant that are modified to provide anchorage for the plant and take in water and nutrients into the plant body, which allows plants to grow taller and faster.
Which leathery-skinned marine echinoderm, of which about 1,786 species are known worldwide, plays a vital ecological role on the sea floor by breaking down detritus as a scavenger?
Sea cucumber are echinoderms from the class Holothuroidea.
Unlike its shelled cousin the snail, this soft-bodied land mollusk gets by with no shell at all, or at most a tiny internal remnant of one — what animal is it?
Slug is a common name for any apparently shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc.
Built from four fused rings, compounds in this class include cholesterol, testosterone, and anti-inflammatory drugs like dexamethasone. What class of compound is it?
Steroid is an organic compound with four fused rings (designated A, B, C, and D) arranged in a specific molecular configuration.
One of the oldest constellations, this zodiac figure once marked the Sun's place at the spring equinox and inspired bull imagery from Sumer to Rome — which northern-sky constellation is it?
Taurus (constellation) (Latin, 'Bull') is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the northern celestial hemisphere.
Found in nature only as an oxide and locked in minerals like rutile and ilmenite, this strong, silvery element bears the name of mythological giants — what is it?
Titanium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ti and atomic number 22.

An oily, amber-colored liquid that's extremely non-volatile and therefore lingers in the environment, this organophosphorus compound was developed for chemical warfare and is lethal in doses of just tens of milligrams — which chemical agent?
VX (nerve agent) is an extremely toxic synthetic chemical compound in the organophosphorus class, specifically, a thiophosphonate.
Native to Eastern and Southern Africa, this large antelope genus includes two species — one black, one blue — whose lineages diverged roughly a million years ago — what animal is it?
Wildebeest (VIL-), also called gnu (NOO or, NEW), are antelopes of the genus Connochaetes and native to Eastern and Southern Africa.

These ear-shaped sea snails wear a shell with a row of breathing holes and a pearly inside, and their flesh is prized as a delicacy worldwide — about 70 species, the biggest a foot long. What are they?
Abalone: Common name for a group of sea snails.
One of the world's few semiaquatic vipers, this venomous pit viper of the southeastern United States coils and displays its fangs when threatened — what is it?
This genus of over 650 succulent species includes a 'true' member long used in pharmaceutical products, native to Africa, Madagascar, and the Arabian Peninsula — which genus?
Aloe: Genus of succulent flowering plants.
Despite helping develop the Soviet Union's thermonuclear weapons, this physicist won the 1975 Nobel Peace Prize for his human-rights activism and was later persecuted as a dissident — who was he?
Andrei Sakharov: Soviet nuclear physicist and human rights activist (1921–1989)
In this severe blood disorder, the bone marrow stops producing red cells, white cells and platelets alike, and about half of all cases have no known cause — what condition is it?
Aplastic anemia: Disease causing insufficient blood cells of all types.

One of its founders, James Keeler, said this science 'seeks to ascertain the nature of the heavenly bodies... rather than their positions or motions' — studying everything from the Sun to the cosmic microwave background. What field is it?
Sitting at the bottom of the forebrain and including the striatum and substantia nigra, this cluster of brain nuclei governs voluntary movement and habit formation — what is it called?
Basal ganglia: Group of subcortical nuclei involved in the motor and reward systems.
Coined by Károly Ereky in 1919, this multidisciplinary field harnesses bacteria, yeast, and plants — often via genetic engineering — to create products and services. What field?
Biotechnology: Use of living systems and organisms to develop or make useful products.
Certified in Canada in 1998, this large-cabin business jet shares its fuselage cross-section with the Challenger 600 and first flew in 1996 — which jet is it?
Bombardier Global Express: Large cabin business jet. The Bombardier Global Express is a large cabin, long-range business jet designed and manufactured by Bombardier Aviation.

Comprising over 250 species that form small colonies of as few as 50 individuals around a single queen, these fuzzy insects were introduced to New Zealand and Tasmania and can sting repeatedly without dying — which insect is it?
Bumblebee: Genus of insect. A bumblebee (or bumble bee, bumble-bee, or humble-bee) is any of over 250 species in the genus Bombus, part of Apidae, one of the bee families.
Designated Alpha Carinae and located some 310 light-years away, this bright giant is the second-brightest star in the night sky, outshone only by Sirius — which star?
Canopus: Brightest star in the constellation of Carina.
A first-generation cephalosporin and β-lactam, this antibiotic can be taken by mouth and treats ear, bone, skin and urinary infections by disrupting bacterial cell-wall growth — what is it?
Cefalexin: Beta-lactam antibiotic. Cefalexin, also spelled cephalexin, is an antibiotic that can treat a number of bacterial infections.
Nicknamed the sea wasp, this Australian box jellyfish is considered the world's most lethal, with venom-laced tentacles up to 10 feet long — which species?
Chironex fleckeri: Species of jellyfish. It has been described as "the most lethal jellyfish in the world", with at least 64 known deaths in Australia from 1884 to 2021.
Discovered in 1969 and sold under the brand name Lotrimin, this azole-class medication treats athlete's foot, ringworm, and oral thrush — what is it?

Native to the western Palearctic and closely related to the rock dove, this large bird feeds mainly on cereals and other plant matter, making it an agricultural pest despite being heavily hunted across its range — what is it?
Common wood pigeon: Species of large, white/green-naped, arboreal bird of Eurasia.
This genus of some 100 low-growing perennials gives us saffron from the dried stigmas of one autumn-blooming species — name the flower genus?
This basic unit of time — averaging 24 hours, or 86,400 seconds — marks one full rotation of the Earth relative to the Sun, and got split into weeks, months, and years. What is it?
Day: Time of one rotation around a planet axis.

Governed since 1961 by the Vienna Convention, this practice of using official representatives to influence international relations became a professionalized field in the early 20th century. What is it?
Diplomacy: Practice of conducting negotiations between representatives of groups or states.
This condition involves involuntarily repeating words or sounds spoken by someone else, and is commonly seen in autism, ADHD, and Tourette syndrome. What is it called?
This branch of zoology, whose name derives from Greek words for 'insect' and 'study,' covers a field that has described over 1.3 million species — which discipline?
The only Old World member of its family to breed in the Northern Hemisphere's temperate zones, this migratory songbird winters in central and southern Africa — what is it?
Eurasian golden oriole: Species of bird.
This Austrian-German automotive engineer built the first gasoline-electric hybrid car and designed the Volkswagen Beetle, but also contributed tanks to Nazi Germany's war effort — who was he?
Ferdinand Porsche: Austrian-born German automotive engineer, inventor (1875–1951)
A type of necrotizing tissue infection affecting the genitals or perineum, this condition most often strikes older men, diabetics or the immunocompromised — what is it called?
Fournier gangrene: Medical condition. It most commonly occurs in older men, but it can also occur both in women and children, diabetics, alcoholics, or the immunocompromised.
Commonly known as snails and slugs, this class is the second-largest in the animal kingdom after insects — what is it called?
Gastropod: Class of molluscs. The fossil record of gastropods extends back to the Late Cambrian.

A colorless, sweet-tasting, syrupy liquid, this sugar alcohol carries three hydroxyl groups, forms the backbone of triglycerides in fats and oils, and doubles as a food-industry sweetener. What is it?

Once nearly all lumped into a single genus before 21st-century research proved that grouping polyphyletic, these grey-and-white seabirds have an older dialect name, 'mew,' echoing their calls — which birds?
Gull: Subfamily of seabirds. The large species take up to four years to attain full adult plumage, but two years is typical for small gulls.
This medical term describes red blood cells rupturing and spilling their contents into the plasma — a process triggered by bacterial toxins or even intense exercise. What is it?
Hemolysis: Rupturing of red blood cells and release of their contents. Hemolysis may occur in vivo or in vitro.
Often called the founder of alpinism and modern meteorology, this Genevan scientist is also credited with building the first successful solar oven — who was he?
Horace Bénédict de Saussure: Genevan scientist and mountaineer (1740–1799)
Marked by dizziness, blurred vision, and fatigue, this cardiovascular condition is generally diagnosed when systolic readings fall under 90 mmHg — what is it?
This ring-shaped structure in the eye controls how much light reaches the retina by adjusting the size of the pupil — and it's also what determines eye color — what is it?
Iris (anatomy): Colored part of an eye.
Once a deputy district attorney in Weld County, Colorado, this now-suspended lawyer served on Donald Trump's 2020 campaign legal team — who is she?
A genus of roughly 125 succulent species native mostly to Madagascar, one of its members became one of the first plants ever sent into space, aboard a Soviet resupply mission in 1979 — which genus?
Kalanchoe: Genus of flowering plants in the stonecrop family.
Named from Greek words for 'hare' and 'form,' this mammalian order splits into rabbits-and-hares on one branch and pikas on the other, totaling around 110 living species — which order?
Cell signaling, homeostasis, metabolism, growth and reproduction are its hallmarks — and every instance of it eventually reaches death. What capacity in matter is this?
This French chemist's discoveries in fermentation and vaccination gave us a heat-treatment process that now bears his name and rabies and anthrax vaccines — who was he?
Louis Pasteur: French chemist, pharmacist and microbiologist (1822–1895)
In larger organizations it stacks into a pyramid, with a board and CEO at the top setting strategy — the broad practice of administering a business or government. What is it?
Management: Coordinating the efforts of persons.
Diagnosis, prognosis, prevention, treatment and palliation of injury and disease — drawing on biomedical science, genetics and technology — define this science and practice. What is it?

Medicine: Diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of illness. Medicine encompasses a variety of health care practices which evolved to maintain and restore health through the prevention and treatment of illness and infection.
This theoretical physicist and science communicator bridged science and science fiction well enough to win a 2021 lifetime achievement award named for Arthur C. Clarke — who is he?
Michio Kaku: American theoretical physicist, futurist and author.
Named in 1883 by a German anthropologist who wrongly believed it was most common among his patients, this bluish congenital birthmark usually fades by puberty — what is it?
Mongolian spot: Type of birthmark. It normally disappears three to five years after birth and almost always by puberty.

When light from distant objects focuses in front of the retina rather than on it, far-away things blur while close ones stay sharp — and spending more time outdoors as a child seems to lower the risk. What's this refractive error?
Myopia: Inability to focus on distant objects.
This small sauropod dinosaur had a wide muzzle packed with more than 500 teeth that were replaced roughly every two weeks — what genus is it?
Native to East Africa and known in some places as 'lady's fingers,' this mallow-family plant is prized for its edible green (sometimes red) seed pods — what is it?

Produced in the hypothalamus and nicknamed for its role in love and social bonding, this peptide hormone also doubles as a pharmaceutical that speeds up childbirth by triggering uterine contractions — what is it?
Oxytocin: Peptide hormone and neuropeptide. Oxytocin is a peptide hormone and neuropeptide normally produced in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary.
Prized wood from this fruit tree's genus, Pyrus, is a favorite material for making high-quality woodwind instruments, and China grows about three-quarters of the world's crop — which fruit?
Pear: Edible fruits from the genus Pyrus.

Combining textual criticism, literary criticism, history, and linguistics, this scholarly field traces its classical roots to the libraries of Pergamum and Alexandria in the 4th century BC — what is it?
Philology: Study of language in historical sources.
Commonly called frangipani, this fragrant flowering shrub native to Mexico and the Caribbean is now a beloved ornamental in Hawaii and desert climates of Arabia — what genus is it?
Plumeria: Genus of flowering plants endemic to the Americas.
Defined as supervising a team to hit all its goals within three primary constraints — scope, time, and budget — what is this discipline?
Project management: Practice of leading the work of a team to achieve goals and criteria at a specified time.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes — including some of the world's largest — must coil around prey and squeeze it into cardiac arrest before swallowing it whole. What is the family?
Pythonidae: Family of snakes. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.

Nicknamed 'the Thud' by its crews, this Mach 2 jet flew most of the early Vietnam War's strike missions and became the only American aircraft ever pulled from combat over unsustainable losses — which plane?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief: US Air Force supersonic fighter-bomber.
Native to tropical Africa and the Indian subcontinent, this medium-sized parrot has established wild populations worldwide after pet-trade escapees adapted brilliantly to city life — which bird?

Rose-ringed parakeet: Species of bird. The rose-ringed parakeet (Psittacula krameri), also known as the ring-necked parakeet, is a medium-sized parrot in the genus Psittacula, of the family Psittaculidae.
This colorless, odorless nerve agent can kill within minutes of inhalation and was banned by the 1993 Chemical Weapons Convention — what is it?
Sarin: Chemical compound and chemical warfare nerve agent.
Domesticated more than 3,000 years ago and prized for having one of the highest oil contents of any seed, which crop is also known as benne?
Sesame: Plant cultivated for its edible seeds.
Known by the E number E211, this white crystalline salt of benzoic acid is a widely used food preservative and pickling agent — what is it?
Sodium benzoate: Common food preservative. It appears as a white crystalline chemical with the formula C6H5COONa.
A luminous ball of plasma held together by its own gravity, the closest example to Earth is the Sun — what celestial object is this?
Star: Large self-illuminated object in space.
Despite the naming confusion with true yams, this starchy tuberous root actually belongs to the morning glory family and hails from tropical Ecuador — which crop?
Sweet potato: Species of edible plant.
More than 30,000 unsaturated hydrocarbons built on (C5H8)n units, produced mostly by plants (especially conifers) and used by some insects as defense — what class of natural compounds is this?
Terpene: Class of oily organic compounds found in plants.
He joined Apple in 1998 to run worldwide operations and stepped up to the top job in 2011 when Steve Jobs resigned — which executive now leads the company?
